questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

__Are you get irritated __if someone disturbs you?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Do you get irritated.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **'Do'** is used to help make the negative and question forms of** present simple** and **past simple tenses**.
 
• For example:
 
 
• **Do** you **know **what time is it?
 
 
 
• **'Do' **is always agreed upon by the **V1** form of verb (look at the example given above). Hence, the use of 'get' (V1) is justified here.
 
• In the interrogative tone, **'are'** is always followed by **'V1 + ing'** form of** verb**.
 
• For example:
 
 
• **Are **you** listening** to what am I saying?
 
 
 
• Hence, options (2) and (3) are incorrect.
 
• The use of **'disturb'** in the latter part of the sentence hints at the fact that the context is in the **present tense**. Hence, 'do' is appropriate here.
 
• The auxiliary verb 'Did' is marked for **past tense**.
 
• For example:
 
 
• You **didn't **say a word to your father, but you **snarled** at me as though I did something wrong.
 
 
 
• Hence, option (4) is grammatically incorrect in this context.

Hence, the correct answer is:*** Do you get irritated*** if someone disturbs you?

__The shopkeeper either offered to __exchange the goods or to refund the money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is-**"The shopkeeper offered either to".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Corelative conjunctions: **These conjunctions are used to connect similar words or elements but they exist in pairs such as 'not only....but also', 'either...or', etc.
 
• These conjunctions connect two** balanced clauses, phrases, or words. **
 
 
• The most common examples of corelative conjunction are : **either\or, neither\nor, such\that, both\and, whether… or.**
 
 
 
• When we use gerunds, prepositions, infinitives, coordinating conjunctions or correlative conjunctions,__ etc., in a sentence, we must use them consistently to maintain the grammatical flow undisturbed.
 
 
• ***Example***: Piya knows not only to cook continental but also baked walnut cakes(incorrect).
 
 
• Piya knows not only to cook continental but also to bake walnut cakes(correct).
 
 
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, **part (a)** has an error of conjunction. 'Either....or' being a conjunction pair shouldn't be misplaced in a sentence.
 
• From the given example and the example, we are sure that the correct placement is **'offered either to'.**
 
• Hence, replace** either offered to** with **'offered either to '**. 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **option 1.**
